maria: quick heads-up — ran a few stress runs isolating prefill vs decode batching (separate queue paths) and hit a nasty perf regression on p99 for streaming chat_small under mixed load. profile dump below, curious if folks see something obvious.

kevin: can you paste the profiler output? was this with the new kernel-selector heuristics or the older static mapping?

maria: new selector + phase-aware scheduler flags on (experiment: `phase_split=true, kernel_auto=true`). profiler snippet:
```
TIMELINE: request 0x7fc...
prefill:  120ms total (kernel_select: 18ms, matmul: 60ms, kv_warm: 14ms, copy: 28ms)
decode:   8ms per token (kernel_select: 2ms, matmul: 4ms, kv_lookup: 1ms)
queue_wait: prefill spikes at 90ms under 200 qps
KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE: 0.72 (drops to 0.46 when prefill+decode interleave)
GPU_UTIL: 78% but tail dominated by kernel_select stalls
```

anil: interesting — kernel_select time looks large. might be expensive fallback path when we split batches (selector recomputes per sub-batch). did you log which kernel was chosen?

maria: yes, logs show frequent `matmul_general->fused_attention_fallback` when prefill batch sizes are small and decode batcher steals GPUs. seems the selector prefers a kernel optimized for long seq but batch sizes end up tiny after split.

olivia: that would explain increased latency — kernel selection overhead + non-optimal kernels. also KV hit rate dip implies cache churn: prefill writes flush entries while decode consumes different key ranges. Did you try pinning KV shards per queue?

maria: tried a quick run with `kv_shard_affinity=true` and it helps hit rate (+0.12) but p99 still +6% vs baseline. suspect continuous batching heuristics still forming pathological tiny prefill batches.

kevin: can we bias batch formation to prefer larger prefill batches when possible? maybe add token_budget weighting so prefill batcher gets token_budget=256 and decode=64 under mixed workloads. that reduces selector churn.

maria: tried token_budget tweak: prefill 224 / decode 64 => p99 improved to +1.8% (still not baseline). profiling shows kernel_select stalls down to 6ms but matmul kernels still run slower for some splits.

anil: another angle: when we separate queues, the kernel cache (per-stream compiled kernels) isn't shared between queues in our runtime, causing recompile or JIT pipeline thrash. can we make kernel cache global across phase queues?

olivia: that could get us big wins, but need to ensure we don't blow memory on devices with constrained allocator. maybe LRU cap + cold-compile fallback.

perf-bot: perf alert: regression detected on job `canary/stream-chat_small` — p99 +12% vs baseline at 2162501100. Related traces: kernel_selector, kv_cache_eviction.

kevin: also saw some cases where decode microbatches are getting scheduled ahead of prefill due to latency aging in queue. maybe age-based priority unfairly favors short decodes and starves prefill. we should add a phase-aware aging multiplier so prefill doesn’t get starved when it produces KV writes.

maria: notes from a quick experiment:
- enable global kernel cache (LRU=128) -> KV hit +0.08, p99 -3%
- token_budget prefill=256 decode=48 -> p99 -4% but throughput down 2%
- phase-aware aging (prefill weight 1.2) -> reduces prefill queue_wait spikes by ~30ms

anil: tradeoff sounds acceptable if we can avoid regressions on SLA. next steps: 1) implement shared kernel cache with LRU cap, 2) make batcher token_budget configurable per-phase in runtime flags, 3) add phase-aware aging multiplier and validate under 3 workload mixes.

olivia: I'll pair with infra to run canary matrix across regions. @maria can you dump a couple full traces (with kernel ids) for the perf team to look at? include `--kernel-verbose` and `--kv-trace=sampled`.

maria: will upload traces to /tmp/prefill-decode-traces-216250 and link once ready. also adding a small repro harness that replays mixed chat+stream workload to reproduce the kernel_select pattern.

kevin: small note — if we globalize kernel cache, ensure eviction doesn't remove kernels currently bound to an in-flight batch. add ref-counting or pin window.

anil: agreed. also consider measuring latency of kernel_select separately vs compile time to know if caching will fully fix it.

maria: thanks — plan to land small flags first (per-phase token_budget, aging multiplier) behind experiment toggles by EOD, then follow-up on kernel cache next week. any objections?

olivia: sounds good. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: action item created: PERF-4823 "Prefill/decode batching separation — kernel cache + phase heuristics" assigned to anil/maria/kevin
